analysis: Examined the head text of docs/developer/test.md (lines 2304-3109, an unchanged-in-this-PR region of test documentation; the PR's actual doc changes are at about lines 3, 1243-1244 and 1808-1811) and the patch to scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py. The doc changes are a date bump, a CI runner-routing reference, and a description of routed-job lane tests, plus a statement that release workflows stay on literal Blacksmith runners. The script change only updates test assertions so that lane jobs (including test-cluster-gpu, test-provider-sdk and test-provider-summary) must declare `needs: [changes, route]` instead of `needs: changes`. These are CI test-assertion and documentation edits, with no runtime provider code, key handling, attestation, WebSocket contract, prefix-cache storage (T-041) or authorization logic touched. They do not alter any threat-model asset, boundary or mitigation. Remaining integration questions, which are outside the supplied evidence: the actual workflow files (.github/workflows/ci.yml etc.) are not in this batch, so whether the macOS jobs now run on routed runners (rather than the literal Blacksmith runners the old doc named) is unverified. Self-hosted or routed runners that build or sign provider artifacts would matter for the signed-artifact/qualification trust contract, but that is not demonstrated here. The assertions only require `needs` ordering, so the test change itself is a safe tightening (jobs wait for routing). The second patch hunk was truncated at the final assertion, but it is consistent with the visible pattern. No security regression identified. A later pass may check the workflow diffs, if any, for runner trust and secret exposure.
